questions.topic: Basic Concepts of Forest and Forestry
questions.stem: Forestry is best described as the
options: cutting down of trees for timber only
planting of food crops in forest areas
study of wild animals in zoos
science and art of establishing, managing and using forests and their resources for the benefit of people
questions.explanation: Forestry covers establishment, protection, management and use of forests, including timber, non-timber products and services.

questions.topic: Basic Concepts of Forest and Forestry
questions.stem: Which of the following is an indirect (protective) benefit of forests?
options: Protection of watersheds and reduction of soil erosion
questions.explanation: Watershed protection, climate regulation and erosion control are indirect benefits; timber, fuelwood and bush meat are direct products.

questions.stem: In a forest ecosystem, fungi and bacteria that break down fallen leaves and dead wood are called
questions.explanation: Decomposers release nutrients from dead organic matter back to the soil.

questions.stem: The process by which forests remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and store carbon in wood is called
questions.explanation: Trees fix CO2 in photosynthesis and store carbon in biomass, helping to reduce climate change.

questions.stem: Which vegetation zone of Nigeria lies along the coast and is dominated by trees with stilt roots and breathing roots?
questions.explanation: Mangroves such as Rhizophora grow in brackish coastal waters with stilt roots and pneumatophores.

questions.stem: The most important factor responsible for the change from rainforest in southern Nigeria to savanna in the north is
options: decrease in the amount and duration of rainfall
questions.explanation: Rainfall decreases and the dry season lengthens northwards, favouring grasses and drought-tolerant trees.

questions.stem: In forestry, wildlife refers to
options: undomesticated animals and plants living in their natural habitats
questions.explanation: Wildlife covers wild fauna (and often flora) living freely in natural habitats.

questions.topic: Endangered, rare and common wildlife species
questions.stem: Which of the following primates is critically endangered and found in the forests of Cross River State, Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Cross River gorilla is the rarest gorilla subspecies, found on the Nigeria-Cameroon border.

questions.stem: The large plank-like roots at the base of many rainforest trees are called
questions.explanation: Buttress roots give support to tall trees growing on shallow soils.

questions.stem: Which of the following features is commonly used to identify forest trees in the field?
options: The colour and smell of the slash (inner bark) and any exudate
The volume of timber in the tree
questions.explanation: Foresters cut a small slash to examine inner bark colour, smell and latex or gum, along with leaves and bark texture.

questions.stem: An area of forest land legally set aside by government for permanent forest production and protection is a
questions.explanation: Forest reserves are constituted under law and form part of the permanent forest estate.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a major cause of deforestation in Nigeria?
options: Clearing of land for agriculture and fuelwood collection
questions.explanation: Farm expansion, fuelwood and charcoal production, logging and urbanisation drive deforestation.

questions.stem: Planting trees on a degraded area in the Sahel savanna where there was no forest before is called
questions.explanation: Afforestation establishes forest on land that was not previously forested.

questions.stem: The taungya system of forest regeneration was first developed in
questions.explanation: Taungya originated in Burma in the nineteenth century and was introduced into Nigeria in the 1920s.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an invasive alien plant that has spread widely in the waterways of the Niger Delta and Lagos lagoon?
questions.explanation: Water hyacinth, native to South America, blocks waterways and harms fisheries.

questions.stem: A forest plantation is established at a spacing of 3 m x 3 m. The number of seedlings required to plant one hectare is about
questions.explanation: Number = 10 000 m^2 / (3 m x 3 m) = 1 111 seedlings.

questions.stem: A fungal disease in which young nursery seedlings collapse at soil level and die is
questions.explanation: Damping off is caused by soil fungi such as Pythium and is favoured by overwatering and crowding.

questions.stem: A nursery manager needs 4 000 polythene pots at ₦25 each and 2 trips of topsoil at ₦30 000 per trip. The total cost of these items is
The removal of some trees from an immature stand to give the remaining trees more space to grow is
questions.explanation: Thinning reduces competition; pruning removes branches from individual trees.

questions.stem: Diameter at breast height (DBH) of a standing tree is measured at a height of
options: the top of the stump after felling
questions.explanation: Breast height is standardised at 1.3 m (1.37 m in some countries) above ground on the uphill side.

questions.stem: Which of the following instruments is used to measure the height of a standing tree?
questions.explanation: Clinometers such as the Suunto and Haga measure angles from which height is calculated.

questions.topic: Meaning, importance and purpose of forest mensuration
questions.stem: A tree has a diameter at breast height of 40 cm. Its basal area, using basal area = (pi x d^2)/4 with pi = 3.142, is about

questions.topic: Enumeration of growing stock and sampling methods
questions.stem: In a forest inventory, ten sample plots of 0.1 ha each contained a total of 450 trees. The estimated number of trees per hectare is
questions.explanation: Total area sampled = 10 x 0.1 = 1 ha, so 450 trees per hectare.

questions.stem: In directional felling, the undercut (notch) is made on the side of the tree
options: facing the intended direction of fall
opposite the intended direction of fall
questions.explanation: The notch faces the direction of fall; the back cut is made from the opposite side, leaving a hinge.

questions.stem: Marking of logs and stumps with a property hammer after felling is done mainly to
options: identify the owner and source of the log and control illegal logging
questions.explanation: Log marks allow tracking from stump to mill and help revenue collection and law enforcement.

questions.stem: The seeds of bush mango (Irvingia gabonensis), sold as "ogbono" in Nigeria, are an example of
questions.explanation: Ogbono seeds are a valuable food NTFP harvested from the wild and from farms.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a secondary (processed) forest product?
questions.explanation: Plywood is manufactured from veneers; logs, firewood and fresh fruits are primary products.

questions.stem: A function of a marketing agency for forest products is to
options: grade, store and transport products from producers to consumers
questions.explanation: Marketing agencies assemble, grade, store, transport, finance and sell forest products.

questions.stem: Kiln drying of sawn timber is preferred to air drying because it
options: increases the moisture content of wood
is faster and allows the moisture content to be controlled
questions.explanation: Kilns reduce moisture quickly and precisely, though they cost more than air seasoning.

questions.stem: The Forestry Research Institute of Nigeria (FRIN) is located in
questions.explanation: FRIN has its headquarters at Jericho Hill, Ibadan, with the Federal College of Forestry also in Ibadan.

questions.stem: A main objective of a national forest policy is to
options: stop all use of forest products
ensure sustainable management of forest resources for present and future generations
questions.explanation: Forest policies aim at sustainable management, conservation and fair use of forest resources.

questions.stem: Under the communal land tenure system,
options: land is owned by the federal government only
land belongs to the community or family and members have rights to use it
individuals can freely sell community land
land is rented from foreign companies
questions.explanation: Communal tenure vests land in the community or family; individuals hold use rights.

questions.stem: The thread-like vegetative structures of a mushroom that grow through the substrate are called
questions.explanation: Hyphae form the mycelium that absorbs food; the fruiting body carries gills that bear spores.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common substrate for growing oyster mushroom (Pleurotus) in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Pleurotus grows on lignocellulose wastes such as sawdust, straw and corn cobs.

questions.stem: The "planting material" used to inoculate a prepared substrate in mushroom production is called
questions.explanation: Spawn is a grain or sawdust carrier fully colonised by mushroom mycelium.

questions.topic: Members of honey bee colony and their roles
questions.stem: The function of drones in a honeybee colony is to
questions.explanation: Drones (males) mate with virgin queens; workers do foraging, guarding and nursing.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most suitable site for an apiary?
options: A quiet place with flowering plants and a water source nearby, away from homes and roads
Near an area where pesticides are sprayed weekly
questions.explanation: Bees need forage and water, and apiaries should be away from people, livestock and pesticides.

questions.topic: Maturity of colony, harvesting and processing
questions.stem: Honey combs are ready for harvesting when
options: most of the cells are sealed (capped) with wax
the cells contain eggs and larvae
the bees have left the hive
questions.explanation: Capped cells contain ripe honey with low moisture that will not ferment.

questions.stem: In a practical class, a student stood 20 m from a tree on level ground and measured the angle of elevation to the tree top as 45 degrees. If the eye level of the student is 1.5 m above the ground, the height of the tree is
questions.explanation: Height = distance x tan(angle) + eye height = 20 x tan 45 + 1.5 = 20 + 1.5 = 21.5 m.

questions.topic: Practical: processing of non-timber forest products
questions.stem: In processing honey after harvest, the wax cappings are first removed from the combs with
questions.explanation: Cappings are sliced off before the combs are spun in an extractor or pressed, and the honey is strained.

questions.stem:
(a) Name the vegetation zones of Nigeria from the coast to the far north. [5 marks]
(b) For any two of the zones named in (a), state two characteristic features of the vegetation and two typical tree species. [8 marks]
(c) Explain three land use practices that threaten the vegetation of the savanna zones, and suggest one way of reducing such threats. [7 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
5 marks: (a) Mangrove/swamp forest; (tropical) rainforest; Guinea savanna (including derived savanna); Sudan savanna; Sahel savanna (montane vegetation on highlands accepted as additional), 1 mark each in correct order
4 marks: (b) First zone: two features (e.g. rainforest - tall trees in several layers, closed canopy, evergreen, buttress roots, many climbers) and two species (e.g. Milicia excelsa, Khaya ivorensis, Triplochiton scleroxylon, Terminalia superba) - 1 mark each
4 marks: (b) Second zone: two features (e.g. Guinea savanna - tall grasses with scattered fire-resistant trees, thick bark, deciduous) and two species (e.g. Parkia biglobosa, Vitellaria paradoxa, Daniellia oliveri, Afzelia africana); mangrove - stilt roots, pneumatophores, Rhizophora, Avicennia - 1 mark each
6 marks: (c) Any three, 2 marks each (practice + explanation): bush burning - destroys seedlings, organic matter and wildlife; overgrazing - removes grass cover and leads to erosion and desertification; shifting cultivation with short fallow - clears woody vegetation repeatedly; fuelwood and charcoal production - removes trees; uncontrolled settlement and urban expansion
1 mark: (c) One way of reducing threats, e.g. controlled early burning/fire tracing, afforestation/shelterbelts, grazing control/reserves, enforcement of forest laws, use of alternative fuels
questions.explanation: (a) Mangrove swamp forest, rainforest, Guinea savanna, Sudan savanna and Sahel savanna. (b) The rainforest has tall evergreen trees in layers with a closed canopy and buttress roots, e.g. iroko and mahogany. The Guinea savanna has tall grasses with scattered fire-resistant trees such as locust bean and shea. (c) Bush burning, overgrazing, shifting cultivation with short fallows and fuelwood cutting degrade savanna vegetation; they can be reduced by controlled early burning, afforestation and grazing control.

questions.stem:
(a) State four factors to consider when selecting a site for a forest nursery. [4 marks]
(b) Describe the procedure for raising Gmelina arborea seedlings in polythene pots from seed sowing to transplanting. [10 marks]
(c) Name three nursery tools and state one use of each. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) Any four, 1 mark each: nearness to a reliable water source; gentle slope and good drainage; fertile topsoil available; accessibility; nearness to planting site; protection from wind, animals and theft; partial shade
2 marks: (b) Collect mature fruits, remove pulp and pre-treat seeds (soaking in water) to hasten germination
2 marks: (b) Fill polythene pots with topsoil (or a mix of topsoil, sand and manure) and arrange in beds
2 marks: (b) Sow 1-2 seeds per pot at shallow depth and water regularly; provide shade
2 marks: (b) Thin to one seedling per pot; weed, control pests and diseases; root prune/shift pots
2 marks: (b) Harden off by reducing shade and watering 2-4 weeks before transplanting at about 3-4 months
6 marks: (c) Any three, 2 marks each (name + use): watering can - watering; hand trowel - lifting seedlings; secateurs - pruning roots/shoots; shade net - shading; wheelbarrow - carrying soil; hand fork - loosening soil; sieve - sieving soil; spade - mixing potting soil
questions.explanation: (a) A nursery site needs water, good drainage, fertile soil, access, protection and nearness to the planting site. (b) Gmelina seeds are extracted, soaked, then sown in soil-filled polythene pots under shade; seedlings are watered, thinned, weeded, protected from pests, root-pruned and hardened off before transplanting. (c) Watering can for watering, trowel for lifting seedlings, secateurs for pruning and shade net for shading.

questions.topic: Enumeration of growing stock and sampling methods
questions.stem:
(a) Explain the following: (i) forest mensuration; (ii) basal area; (iii) forest inventory. [6 marks]
(b) A tree has a diameter at breast height of 60 cm. Calculate its basal area in m^2 (take pi = 3.142). [4 marks]
(c) A log is 8 m long and has a mid-diameter of 50 cm. Using Huber's formula, V = (pi x d^2 / 4) x L, calculate its volume in m^3 to two decimal places. [4 marks]
(d) Name three instruments used in forest mensuration and state the use of each. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) Forest mensuration: the measurement of trees, logs and forest stands (diameter, height, volume, growth) for planning and management
2 marks: (a)(ii) Basal area: the cross-sectional area of a tree stem at breast height (1.3 m), or the sum of these for a stand per hectare
2 marks: (a)(iii) Forest inventory: systematic collection of data on the quantity, quality and distribution of trees/forest resources in an area
1 mark: (b) d = 0.60 m; BA = pi x d^2 / 4
1 mark: (b) = 3.142 x 0.36 / 4
2 marks: (b) = 0.283 m^2 (0.2828)
1 mark: (c) Mid cross-sectional area = 3.142 x 0.5^2 / 4 = 0.1964 m^2
1 mark: (c) V = 0.1964 x 8
2 marks: (c) = 1.57 m^3
6 marks: (d) Any three, 2 marks each: diameter tape/calipers - measure diameter; clinometer/hypsometer/Haga altimeter/Abney level - measure tree height; relascope - basal area and heights; measuring tape - length of logs and plot boundaries; increment borer - age and growth rate; prism/wedge - basal area
questions.explanation: (a) Forest mensuration is the measurement of trees and stands; basal area is the cross-sectional area at breast height; a forest inventory is a systematic survey of forest resources. (b) BA = 3.142 x 0.60^2 / 4 = 0.283 m^2. (c) Mid-area = 3.142 x 0.25 / 4 = 0.196 m^2; V = 0.196 x 8 = 1.57 m^3. (d) Diameter tape for diameter, clinometer for height and increment borer for age and growth.

questions.stem:
(a) State four pre-harvesting activities in timber harvesting. [4 marks]
(b) Describe the procedure for felling a tree using a chainsaw. [8 marks]
(c) State four safety measures to be observed during timber harvesting. [4 marks]
(d) Explain two effects of poor harvesting practices on the forest. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) Any four, 1 mark each: forest inventory/enumeration and tree marking for felling; obtaining permits/licences; planning and constructing access roads and skid trails; demarcation of felling area; checking for hazards; mobilising equipment and trained crew
2 marks: (b) Determine the direction of fall considering lean, wind, crown shape and obstacles; clear the base and plan escape routes
2 marks: (b) Make the undercut (notch) on the side facing the direction of fall, about one-quarter to one-third of the diameter
2 marks: (b) Make the back cut on the opposite side slightly above the base of the notch, leaving a hinge of uncut wood
2 marks: (b) Shout a warning, move away along the escape route as the tree falls; then delimb and cross-cut into logs
4 marks: (c) Any four, 1 mark each: wear protective equipment (helmet, visor, ear muffs, chaps, boots, gloves); only trained operators; keep a safe distance (twice tree height) from others; check and maintain equipment; avoid felling in strong winds; first aid kit available; never work alone
4 marks: (d) Any two, 2 marks each: damage to residual trees and seedlings reduces regeneration; soil compaction and erosion along skid trails; wastage of timber through poor cutting; loss of wildlife habitat; siltation of streams
questions.explanation: (a) Inventory and tree marking, permits, road and skid-trail planning, demarcation and preparation of equipment. (b) Choose the felling direction and escape routes, cut a notch facing the fall, make the back cut slightly higher leaving a hinge, warn others and retreat, then delimb and cross-cut. (c) Protective equipment, trained operators, safe distances, maintained equipment and no felling in strong wind. (d) Poor harvesting damages residual trees, compacts and erodes soil and wastes timber.

questions.stem:
(a) State four importance of mushrooms. [4 marks]
(b) Describe the steps involved in growing oyster mushroom on sawdust in polythene bags. [10 marks]
(c) State three conditions necessary for the fruiting of mushrooms and three post-harvest handling practices. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) Any four, 1 mark each: source of protein, vitamins and minerals; low-fat food suitable for people with diabetes and heart disease; medicinal value; source of income/employment; recycling of agricultural and wood wastes; spent substrate used as manure/feed
2 marks: (b) Prepare substrate: mix sawdust with supplements (e.g. rice/wheat bran, lime) and water to the right moisture
2 marks: (b) Fill into heat-resistant polythene bags, plug the necks and pasteurise/sterilise by steaming
2 marks: (b) Cool and inoculate with spawn under clean conditions
2 marks: (b) Incubate in a dark, clean room until the mycelium fully colonises the bags (spawn running), usually 3-5 weeks
2 marks: (b) Open or slit the bags and move to the cropping room for fruiting; harvest when caps are fully formed but before edges curl up
3 marks: (c) Conditions, any three, 1 mark each: high relative humidity (about 80-90%); moderate temperature; some light (indirect); good ventilation/fresh air; adequate moisture in substrate
3 marks: (c) Post-harvest, any three, 1 mark each: harvest by twisting gently; clean and sort; pack in ventilated containers; keep cool/refrigerate; sun- or oven-dry for longer storage; sell quickly
questions.explanation: (a) Mushrooms are nutritious, medicinal, generate income and recycle wastes. (b) Supplemented sawdust is bagged, pasteurised, cooled and inoculated with spawn, incubated in the dark until colonised, then opened in a humid cropping room and harvested before the caps curl. (c) Fruiting needs high humidity, moderate temperature, indirect light and fresh air; after harvest mushrooms are cleaned, packed in ventilated containers and kept cool or dried.

questions.stem:
(a) Name the three members of a honeybee colony and state two roles of each. [9 marks]
(b) State five routine management practices in an apiary. [5 marks]
(c) Name three products of beekeeping and give one use of each. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Queen
2 marks: (a) Queen: lays eggs; produces pheromones that keep the colony together
1 mark: (a) Drone
2 marks: (a) Drone: mates with the virgin queen; helps maintain hive temperature (any two accepted)
1 mark: (a) Worker
2 marks: (a) Worker: collects nectar and pollen; builds comb; feeds larvae; guards the hive; cleans the hive (any two)
5 marks: (b) Any five, 1 mark each: regular inspection of hives; controlling pests such as ants, wax moths and hive beetles; keeping the apiary clean and clearing weeds; providing water nearby; checking for diseases; harvesting at the right time; protecting hives from fire, theft and animals; record keeping; providing shade
6 marks: (c) Any three, 2 marks each (product + use): honey - food/medicine; beeswax - candles, polish, cosmetics; propolis - medicine/antiseptic; royal jelly - food supplement/cosmetics; pollen - food supplement; bee venom - medicine
questions.explanation: (a) The queen lays eggs and controls the colony with pheromones; drones mate with the queen; workers forage, build comb, feed larvae and guard the hive. (b) Routine inspection, pest and disease control, clean surroundings, water supply, protection from fire and theft, timely harvesting and records. (c) Honey is food and medicine, beeswax makes candles and cosmetics, and propolis is used as an antiseptic.
